 This Motor Accident Claims Appeal Having Been Finally Heard
On 10.04.2025, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following:
 Maca No. 3345 Of 2014

 Judgment
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.1652 of 2009 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Ernakulam, is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter
referred

to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 23.07.2009.

According to the petitioner, on 23.07.2009 at about 05.05 p.m., while he was riding a motorcycle along Edappally - Vytilla bypass road, a lorry bearing Registration No.TN-28/AB 30 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down.
As a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.10,14,000/- limited to Rs.10,00,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A18 and C1.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,50,816/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Sreeram.H vs Jyothi Lakshmi .K (Deleted) on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35966948/
2 Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9 . Heard Sri.P.M.Joshi, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.P Jacob Mathew, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
As per the claim petitioner, the petitioner was working as a service man in BOSCH Ltd, earning Rs.3,600/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.4,000/-.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the MACA NO. 3345 OF 2014 2025:KER:31622 decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co.
Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the 2009 will come to Rs.7,000/-.

Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co.
Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the learned counsel prayed for fixing the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.7,000/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

Since the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2009 will come to Rs.7,000/-, in order to award just and reasonable compensation, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra), the notional income of the petitioner is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.7,000/-.

12. In the accident the petitioner sustained fracture dislocation left shoulder, lacerated wound left knee, left chest contusion, fracture right upper incisor and lacerated wound below nose, fracture greater tuberosity left humerus, comminuted fracture left maxilla, fracture left zygoma, fracture left body of mandible and grossly destructed 7 teeth.

13. Ext.C1 disability certificate issued by the medical board shows that the petitioner suffered 3%
permanent physical disability.
The Tribunal, after examining the petitioner fixed the permanent disability of the petitioner at 6%, which is not under challenge.
Therefore, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is accepted at 6%, as fixed by the Tribunal.
On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 29 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 17, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.1,19,952/-.
15.
Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.35,000/-.
In the accident, the petitioner sustained very serious injuries including four fractures and he lost his 7 teeth.
He has also undergone two surgeries and implant was removed on 18.06.2010, about one year after the accident.
Therefore, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 12 months.

Therefore, towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.84,000/- (7000 x 12 Sreeram.H vs Jyothi Lakshmi .K (Deleted) on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35966948/
3 months).
16.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.2,000/- was awarded.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner,
the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
17. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 13 days in three spells and in the meantime he had undergone two surgeries also.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage MACA NO. 3345 OF 2014 2025:KER:31622 of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings' and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.75,000/- and Rs.10,000/- respectively.
18. Towards the head 'loss of amenities', no amount was granted by the Tribunal.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I am inclined to grant Rs.1,00,000/- towards the head 'loss of amenities'.
19. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

20. Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.6,30,736/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

3 Extra nourishment 2,000 10,000  5 Attendant expenses 4500 4500  MACA NO. 3345 OF 2014  2025:KER:31622  6
Medical expenses 2,32,784 2,32,784

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.6,30,736/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Thirty Thousand Seven Hundred and Thirty Six only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation,
excluding interest for a period of 110 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal,
with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner,
excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
